plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree that produces fragrant five-petaled blossoms on bare branches before leaves emerge. It is prized in East Asian gardens and is often celebrated at ume festivals as a harbinger of spring.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (January to March)
plants.location: Japan, China, Korea; cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms are a symbol of perseverance in East Asian culture because they bloom in cold weather, sometimes while snow is still on the ground.

plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: A small bulbous perennial with drooping, bell-shaped white flowers marked with green on the inner petals. It carpets woodlands and gardens in naturalized drifts and is one of the earliest flowers of the year.
plants.location: Europe, from the Pyrenees to Ukraine; naturalized in the UK and North America
plants.funFact: Snowdrops produce a compound called galantamine, which is used in medication to treat symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A striking evergreen shrub with giant flower heads surrounded by colorful bracts, adapted to the fynbos ecosystem. Its large blooms are pollinated by birds and small mammals, and it is South Africa's national flower.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to early autumn in the Southern Hemisphere, with blooms often occurring from late winter through spring
plants.location: Western and Southern Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: Proteas are among the most ancient flowering plants, with a lineage that dates back roughly 300 million years to the supercontinent Gondwana.

plants.name: Acacia dealbata
plants.description: A fast-growing evergreen tree with feathery silver-blue foliage and dense, fluffy clusters of fragrant yellow pompom flowers. It is widely planted in Mediterranean climates and used in the cut flower trade.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (January to March in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Southeastern Australia; naturalized in the Mediterranean, the French Riviera, and parts of California
plants.funFact: The town of Mandelieu-la-Napoule on the French Riviera holds an annual Mimosa Festival in February to celebrate the blooming of this tree.
